title: Interactive Natural Language Processing
measurement_description: The paper is a broad survey of Interactive Natural Language Processing (iNLP) and does not empirically measure or evaluate any aspects of faith or religion. Religion is only briefly mentioned theoretically as a demographic category vulnerable to social bias (e.g., job applicants hiding their religion) that language models might inherit and amplify.
findings: The paper does not present specific findings related to religion, as it is a survey on iNLP. It only briefly notes that language models trained on large-scale web corpora can inherit and amplify societal biases, including discrimination and stereotypes based on religion.
